findings.title: Backup vault is selected without a supported protected workload or policy boundary.
findings.finding: The design adds a Microsoft.DataProtection/backupVaults resource and lists Azure Backup vault as part of SBB-16, but the reviewed contracts do not bind that vault to a Microsoft-supported protected workload, backup policy, restore path or owner. Azure SQL Database is already covered by service automated PITR/LTR/failover patterns; treating a Data Protection Backup vault as a generic regional backup control is not implementation-ready and can lead AFF-4 to deploy an unsupported or unused recovery component.
evidence: 3-azure-design/stratton-azure-design.md:243 lists bv-stratton-prd-<regionRole>-<loc> as a Regional backup vault.
3-azure-design/stratton-design-catalogue.json:219 lists Azure SQL automated backups, Azure Backup vault and Blob versioning/soft delete in SBB-16.
3-azure-design/stratton-design-catalogue.json:316 selects Microsoft.DataProtection/backupVaults without naming protected data sources or backup policies.
3-azure-design/evidence/stratton-operations-reliability-contract.json:19 correctly uses Azure SQL automated PITR backups for SQL state but does not explain what the Backup vault protects.
Microsoft Learn, Backup vaults overview, states Backup vaults hold backup data for supported newer workloads such as Azure Blob and Azure Database for PostgreSQL servers.
Microsoft Learn, Azure SQL Database automated backups overview, states Azure SQL Database automatically creates full, differential and transaction log backups and supports PITR/LTR.

findings.owner: AFF-3 with AFF-4 handoff owner and Business Continuity
findings.boundedRemediation: Either remove the Backup vault from SBB-16/resource inventory, or explicitly bind it to supported workloads such as Blob backup with policy, retention, restore, region and ownership details. Keep Azure SQL recovery on automated backups/LTR/failover groups unless a supported Azure Backup workload is introduced.

findings.title: Private-only Application Gateway opt-in is not carried as an AFF-4 fail-closed input.
findings.finding: The design correctly chooses a private-only Application Gateway WAF_v2 ingress, but the handoff does not carry the required subscription feature opt-in/registration check as a fail-closed implementation input. Microsoft Learn says private IP-only Application Gateway v2 controls are generally available and production-supported, but use requires opting in to the experience; missing this gate could block deployment late.

verdictRationale: One unresolved MAJOR feasibility/implementation-readiness finding remains: the selected Backup vault resource is not bound to a supported protected workload or recovery policy. Under the AFF-A severity rules, an unresolved major finding yields DIVERGES. The additional minor Application Gateway opt-in gap is bounded but still requires subject remediation if the design is revised.

requiredActions.action: Remediate AFFA-P3-R1-MAJ-001 by removing the unbound Backup vault or binding it to supported workload-specific backup and restore policies; do not use Backup vault as a generic SQL backup mechanism.
Remediate AFFA-P3-R1-MIN-001 by carrying private-only Application Gateway opt-in/registration evidence into AFF-4 inputs or preflight checks.
Regenerate affected Phase 3 artifacts and the canonical manifest after remediation, then re-run AFF-A and AFF-B over the same unchanged regenerated manifest.
Do not open the human Phase 3 approval gate for this manifest; DIVERGES blocks it.
